title: One Force Behind Light and Magnets
question: How can lightning, compasses and light all be one thing?
hook: The glue in every atom is also what carries a radio signal across the planet.
idea: Electric and magnetic effects are one interaction, working through fields and shaping atoms, chemistry and light.

beats.prompt: Ancient people noticed lightning, static sparks and iron ore that pulls on compasses. What did later scientists find about these?

choices.label: Electrical and magnetic phenomena are related and can form waves
choices.feedback: Right idea, and this is the real answer.

choices.label: They are three unrelated curiosities with no common cause
choices.feedback: It seems natural since they look different, but scientists showed the phenomena were related.

choices.label: Only lightning is real, and magnetism is an illusion of iron
choices.feedback: Magnetic interactions are real and part of the same interaction.

beats.explain: In the 18th and 19th centuries scientists found mathematical relationships and showed electrical and magnetic phenomena were related, creating self-sustaining electromagnetic waves.

beats.prompt: Match each electromagnetic role to what it does.
pairs: Include visible light, X-rays and radio waves
Describe electric and magnetic influence at a place and time
beats.explain: The same interaction binds atoms, builds molecules and travels as waves, and fields are the mathematical way to describe it.

beats.prompt: Sort each into the group it belongs to.
groups: Unified as electroweak at high energy
items: Unified as electroweak at high energy
Unified as electroweak at high energy
beats.explain: At high energy the weak and electromagnetic forces merge into one electroweak interaction, while friction and contact forces are non-fundamental, derived from the four fundamental forces.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Electromagnetism acts between electrically charged particles.
So it is the strongest of the four fundamental forces.
Still, it dominates how atoms and molecules interact.
beats.explain: Electromagnetism is the second strongest of the four known fundamental forces, not the strongest.
